profile.headline: Principal Software Engineer - Machine Learning
profile.summary: I am a Master's student studying Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Texas at Austin. My studies are primarily directed towards Data Science, and I expect to graduate December 2021. I have taken undergraduate data science courses and I am currently enrolled in graduate-level probability, convex optimization, and machine learning courses.

positions.title: Cloud Engineering Intern
positions.description: I conducted feasibility studies for correctable to uncorrectable DRAM error prediction in customer server data. The telemetry data was stored in Google Cloud Platform and I used BigQuery and Google Cloud Storage to extract, process, and save the data. I also wrote a Python script to compute server DIMM corrections per second with multithreading and a progress bar.

positions.title: Data Science Intern
positions.description: I worked with Micron's DRAM data science team to improve a model that clusters 2d histograms of validation results (shmoo plots) and identifies statistical differences in shmoo plots across different groups. I also built a dashboard using streamlit in Python to summarize the results and to help visualize the shmoo data.

positions.title: Student Technician
positions.description: I worked with the unmanned underwater vehicle team to train an object clustering model. I used an unsupervised algorithm called information invariant clustering to train a model to cluster sonar images of objects detected in the water.

company.name: Applied Research Laboratories, The University of Texas at Austin

positions.title: DEG Design Intern
positions.description: I designed a non-binary row decoding scheme that is compatible with concurrent Vt compensation and then built the circuit schematics in Cadence Virtuoso and verified the logical functionality of the circuitry in Verilog. I also coded a GUI with Python to help with calculating address mappings, querying row address location within a bank, minimizing circuit logic equations, and creating testvectors for Verilog simulations. Towards the end of the internship, I created a Powerpoint animation to visualize a potential rowhammer solution and its weaknesses.

positions.title: Student Technician
positions.description: I worked with the unmanned underwater vehicle team, I performed orthogonal regression that accounts for outliers with a modified RANSAC algorithm in Python.

company.name: Applied Research Laboratories, The University of Texas at Austin

positions.title: Technology and Operations Intern
positions.description: I interned in NXP's Global New Product Introduction (NPI) Test Center. I used Python to create a new automated parser for prober PMI and PTPA logs that is 55 times faster than the old parser. The parser also writes the data to a Microsoft SQL Server database and is accompanied by a GUI tool to query data from the database. For my second project, I executed a copper pillar high temperature solder transfer and bump deformation experiment using a Teradyne Ultraflex tester and Accretech UF3000EX and UF3000EX-e probers. After each test, I inspected and documented the probe card needles and wafer bumps with a Nikon MM-800 measuring scope and DS-Fi2 camera.

positions.title: Student Technician
positions.description: I worked with the unmanned underwater vehicle team analyzing geopositional data collected by sonar. I used Python to classify objects detected by sonar by giving each object a score based on certain variables.  I evaluated the performance of the classification algorithm using a receiver operator characteristic (ROC) curve.
